messages:
sam: Hi team — quick question as I'm landing my first change: what's our recommended PR size and branching pattern? I want to avoid rework and make it easy for reviewers.

mira: Hey @sam :wave: — short answer: keep PRs focused (ideally one logical change). We aim for <300 LOC wherever possible, but more importantly 1 cohesive purpose per PR.

mira: Branching: feature/<your-name>/<short-desc> for work-in-progress, then feature/<your-name>/final-<ticket> when ready. We avoid long-lived feature branches.

mira: Review process: add the relevant reviewer team (e.g., @eng-runtime or @devex) and ping one person for a quick sanity check. If it's infra or infra-adjacent, include @eng-infra.

olivia: +1. Include a short checklist in the PR body so reviewers know what to focus on (behavior change, perf impact, migration steps). Example snippet I use: 
```
Summary: one-line
Test plan: unit + integration
Risk: low/medium/high
Rollout: instant / gradual
Files changed rationale: short bullets
```

olivia: Also call out if this touches model-serving hotpaths (latency/kv cache) — tag @eng-runtime.

devex-bot: [CI] PR #1234 — lint: passed ✅, unit tests: 38 passed, integration: running... (ETA ~5m)

taylor: Local commands that help catch style issues early: 
`./tools/lint` and `./tools/check-format` before pushing. If you want to run just the tests affected by your change: `pytest -k "path/to/file"`

taylor: If the change is risky, mark it with label `risk/high` and request an approval from a senior oncall. Small UX/Docs-only PRs can be `size/xs` and fast-tracked.

mira: Where to find docs: https://intranet.redwood/dev/contrib/pr-guidelines and the style guide is at https://intranet.redwood/dev/contrib/style.md — read the commit message conventions and the HTTP API style section.

sam: This is great, thanks! One last q: who usually does the first review for new devs?

olivia: @mira or @taylor will usually take the first look if available. Also volunteer for pairing reviews — mention "review buddy" in the PR if you want a guided walkthrough. :thumbsup:

sam: Perfect — I'll open a small PR now and add the checklist. Thanks all!
